---
title: "Earth2Studio.jl"
---

## Overview

**Earth2Studio.jl** is a thin Julia wrapper around [NVIDIA's earth2studio](https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio) Python package for AI-powered weather and climate forecasting. It uses [PythonCall.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/PythonCall.jl) to expose the full `earth2studio` Python API — data sources, prognostic and diagnostic models, perturbations, IO backends, run workflows, and verification statistics — as native Python objects you can call from Julia.

The package itself is intentionally minimal: it imports `earth2studio` and its top-level submodules, and re-exports them as `Py` references. All functionality lives in the upstream Python package.

## Quickstart

Install Earth2Studio.jl:

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add("Earth2Studio")
```

The Conda environment managed by [CondaPkg.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/CondaPkg.jl) installs Python, NumPy, and xarray. The `earth2studio` Python package itself must be added to your project (extras pick which models you want):

```julia
using CondaPkg
CondaPkg.add_pip("earth2studio")            # base
CondaPkg.add_pip("earth2studio[fcn,pangu]") # with model extras
```

Then call into the Python API:

```julia
using Earth2Studio

ds = data.ARCO()
model = models.px.FCN.load_model(models.px.FCN.load_default_package())
backend = io.ZarrBackend("/tmp/forecast.zarr")
result = run.deterministic(time, 10, model, ds, backend)
```

See the [Tutorial](tutorial.qmd) for a longer walkthrough of the interop patterns.
